findings.where: Article specimen (heading, standfirst, body, pull quote), and the article / blog pages it stands for
findings.fault: Long reading text is set light-on-mid-blue, in Overpass Light/Regular, with the 20 mm blueprint grid lines running through the paragraphs. That suits a title block, but a full PPP-law article of several screens will be tiring to read, and the specimen only shows three short paragraphs, so the cost is hidden.
findings.who_objects: The bank official, who reads one of Mark's articles to judge his thinking before writing to him. Faint lines crossing every line of reversed text make a long, careful read harder, and the brief names Read as a mode the look must serve.

findings.where: Hero drawing, the amber hatch in the third bay, against the WRITE TO MARK button; the palette tile gives Sodium Amber two jobs ('daylight in the drawing, and the one action')
findings.fault: The colour kept for the one action is also used as decoration in the drawing. In the overview and on the first screen, the eye goes to the amber hatch before it finds the amber button below. The button no longer has the view's strongest colour to itself.
findings.who_objects: The visitor scanning for what to do next, whose eye goes to an amber patch in a picture first. Under the house carrier rule the primary action's colour is reserved, so decoration may not take it.

findings.where: Nav bar title-block cells 'DRAWING MMM-GA-001' and 'SCALE NTS' (desktop right end; phone top row beside the logo)
findings.fault: Two of the nav's cells hold static drawing codes. They use the same bordered cells and spaced capitals as PROFILE / ARTICLES / BLOG / CONTACT, so they look like nav items but do nothing (parts.txt p6, p7 static). On phone they take half the top row and squeeze the logo, while the real links drop to a second row.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who taps 'MMM-GA-001' expecting a page, or who reads the nav for where to go and meets codes that mean nothing to them. Mark's 'not busy' value also asks for less chrome than this.

findings.where: Hero identity line under the name ('LONGITUDINAL SECTION A-A • SCALE NTS'), the circled 'A' beside the name, and the drawing labels 'NTS', 'EQ', '±0.00'
findings.fault: The drawing conceit spills into the text that says who Mark is. Grouped by proximity, his title reads 'Infrastructure advisor, longitudinal section A-A, scale NTS'. At a glance the circled 'A' reads as an avatar initial or a grade, and on phone the line wraps with a bullet stranded at its end.
findings.who_objects: The senior official reading the first screen literally. The second line of Mark's identity is jargon that tells them nothing and reads as a gimmick, which works against the calm, confident, no-slogan voice Mark asks for.

findings.where: Hero drawing, the aqueduct presented as a dimensioned engineering section
findings.fault: The logo's stylised crescent arches are framed as a technical section, with EQ dimensions, centre lines, a datum and earth hatch. Read as a drawing, the structure could not stand: the first arch's left leg ends in mid-air and the arches do not visibly bear the deck. A stray S-curve rising from the ground at the far right is unexplained and looks like a leftover line.
findings.who_objects: An infrastructure professional at a development bank, who reads section drawings for a living. A drawing that claims engineering precision and shows an unbuildable structure undercuts the expertise it is meant to signal.

findings.where: Nav bar logo (top left, desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The mark and the 'MMM INFRA' wordmark appear reversed in near-white. The logo's own colours are grey #404040 arches and a blue #0070C0 wordmark, and the brief holds no white version. A reversed version is a version the client does not hold.
findings.who_objects: Mark, whose logo the brief says is never redrawn. The house rule says a version the client does not hold is made only with the client's yes, so this direction depends on a ruling not yet given.

findings.where: WRITE TO MARK button (hero), and the page's end, which has no footer
findings.fault: The only contact route is a mailto button. Mark's email address appears nowhere as text, and the page ends on the motion-sketch box with no footer address. The arrow on the button suggests it goes to a page, but it opens a mail program.
findings.who_objects: An official on a locked-down work machine or webmail, where mailto opens nothing or the wrong client. They are left with no address to copy at the one moment they decided to get in touch.

findings.where: First screen as a whole (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: No photograph of Mark appears, and no place is held for one. The tile never shows how a portrait sits on the diazo-blue ground, though client value 3 ('Mark is seen') applies to every direction. The person is named but never shown.
findings.who_objects: The visitor choosing an individual advisor, who wants to see the real person. Mark, too, asked that he be seen, and a blueprint ground is the direction where a photograph is hardest to place.

findings.fault: There is no third-party proof and no link out to work that named bodies host (for example a lecture venue or a World Bank publication). The only standing shown is Mark's own line about his former role.
findings.who_objects: A procurement-minded official, who looks for checkable outside evidence before shortlisting. This must be filled with real, consented proof only, never invented.

findings.where: Type pair note against the article specimen heading; article date '18 September 2024' against lecture meta 'Lecture • 2026-04-23 · PDF'
findings.fault: The type spec says headings are ExtraBold tracked capitals, but the article title is set in mixed case. Dates use two formats on one page, and the lecture line mixes two separators (• and ·). The written rules and the specimen disagree.
findings.who_objects: Angélique, adding a post or a PDF, who cannot tell which form is the rule. A careful reader may also notice inconsistent dates on a lawyer's site.

findings.where: Lecture card in the article specimen (bordered box with underlined title and meta)
findings.fault: The whole box has a border like a card target, but only the title is a link (p35). Clicking the 'PDF' meta or the box itself does nothing.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who clicks 'PDF' to get the lecture and gets no response.

findings.fault: A button is styled as underlined capitals, which is the link's reserved look, so it reads as navigation rather than an action on the spot.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who expects to be taken somewhere and instead sees the drawing replay, a small mismatch between look and action.

findings.where: Small caption text throughout the tile (palette notes, texture caption, type-pair notes, motion notes)
findings.fault: Small light-weight text reversed out of mid-blue looks thin and fragile next to the heavy white linework. The notes read as faint afterthoughts.
findings.who_objects: A senior reader, often older, who squints at thin reversed small text. The quiet notes are the ones that explain things.
